sources.note: Nothing. Read in full (122k chars). It is an annotated bibliography of 120-odd Marist mission prints 1910s-1960s; each entry gives title, imprint, size and 'Langue X'. The only occurrence of 'accent' is typographic (no. 11: 'l'absence de caracteres portant des accents dans l'oeil utilise' = the typeface had no accented sorts). No phonology, orthography notes, stress or tone for any language.

sources.note: No phonology content: the chapter goes straight from the classified wordlist (§§187-188) to numerals, pronouns, particles, adjectives, verbs and clause types (§§189-206) and three text samples (§207). The only occurrence of 'Betonung' in the whole Abhandlung is in the Sesake chapter (yes/no questions distinguished only by intonation).

sources.citation: Naitoro, Katerina. 2019. Morphs in search of meaning: Southeast Solomonic transitive morphology in diachronic perspective. PhD thesis, The Australian National University. (Bauro data: author's own fieldnotes, Honiara, Dec 2014-May 2015 and Jan-Apr 2016; Appendix A p. 355.)
sources.note: No phonology chapter; first-hand Bauro verb data (73 mentions, dozens of transcribed forms) used for transitive-suffix comparison only. The one passage on stress (p. 219) is about Boumaa Fijian and a general remark that SES descriptions rarely discuss stress; nothing language-specific for Bauro.

sources.citation: SIL Solomon Islands [SITAG]. 2019. Three Tairaha [bxa]-English talking storybooks on Bloom Library: 'Na Niu / The Coconut' (Scholar Sugera; English Lorae Brignall), 'Tairaha Language Easter Story', 'Pusi ne Paparu Arighuia na Hinua / The Cat Walks Around the Village'. Copyright SIL, Solomon Islands, CC BY 4.0; Tairaha audio narration included.
sources.note: Story text and credits only; no alphabet page, orthography note or prosodic marking. Value: (i) proves a current SIL orthography (hence an unpublished orthography/phonology statement by the Brignall/SITAG team almost certainly exists - the works still to obtain to request); (ii) the embedded Tairaha audio narration of known text is open material for a future acoustic check of stress placement.

sources.note: Nothing on stress; establishes the autonym Tairaha and the district name Bwauro, and that a SITAG/Wycliffe translation team exists (possible unpublished phonology/orthography material).

sources.citation: Fox, Charles E. 1978. Arosi Dictionary. Revised edition with English-Arosi index prepared by Mary Craft. Pacific Linguistics C-57. Canberra: The Australian National University. iv+602 pp. (Bauro cognates tagged 'B.' in c. 1,960 entries; first edition: Arosi-English Dictionary, PL C-11, 1970.)
sources.note: Embedded Bauro wordlist without accent marks or any prosodic remark; the editors' preface has no phonology; the two accent notes in the volume ('accent in these three words is on second vowel, ratárata'; 'accent mwadí'u') concern Arosi headwords. Wordlist-only data for Bauro, not a statement.

sources.citation: Snyders, J. (avec une introduction d'Andre-Georges Haudricourt). 1968. Le langage par tambours a San Cristoval, British Solomon Islands. Journal de la Societe des Oceanistes 24: 133-138. DOI 10.3406/jso.1968.2239. (Reprinted as ch. 62 in Sebeok & Umiker-Sebeok eds. 1976, Speech Surrogates: Drum and Whistle Systems, part 2.)
sources.note: No word-stress statement. The drum surrogate encodes vowel quality syllable by syllable (a = low stroke, other vowels = high), not lexical pitch or stress; Haudricourt's introduction adds (p. 133) 'aux Nouvelles-Hebrides et aux iles Salomon, ou l'on a signale l'emploi de messages tambourines, on n'a pas trouve jusqu'ici de langues a tons' and (p. 134) that here 'le timbre de la voyelle remplace le ton'. Indirect evidence that the language is non-tonal; silent on accent placement.

sources.citation: Fox, C. E. 1947. Phonetic laws in Melanesian languages. Journal of the Polynesian Society 56(1): 58-118.
sources.note: Nothing on Bauro accent. Bauro is cited for segmental facts only (its y ~ velar fricative, first heard 'as h' by Drew and Fox; c. 20 B. cognates such as 'B., rito, sun', 'B., hiqu' star, 'Bauro uragi, ragi' marry). The single accent remark in the article concerns Arosi: 'N.B.-Wherever in Arosi the conditional ma is used the accent falls on the second syllable, the first syllable of the word base.'
